payload.name: Broaden retrieval for shared-activity questions
payload.description: When a question asks what two people do together, do not restrict the search to queries containing both names and the word 'together'; also search each person's individual activities because joint activities are often stored under one participant.
content: If a question asks what two people do together (e.g., 'What do X and Y do together?'), do not rely only on a query that includes both names and 'together'; that over-constrains retrieval and misses memories stored under one person.

Run additional searches using each person's name alone with generic activity terms (e.g., '[X] activities', '[Y] hobbies'), and include memory kinds event, preference, and profile so individual activity memories can surface.

Before answering 'no information available', inspect whether any retrieved memory about one person's activities could describe an activity shared with the other person, and if needed retry with broader terms or higher top_k.

solves: The retrieval failed because the query was built entirely around both participant names plus 'together', so memories stored under only one participant's activities were not retrieved. This over-constraining pattern recurs whenever a question asks what two people do together, but the memory records the activity for one person. The rule applies to future shared-activity or joint-hobby questions: supplement pair-specific wording with per-person activity searches and generic activity terms before concluding the information is absent.
